diagram_math_checks.evidence: Using the item Statement f(z)=z+mu conjugate(z) and F3, substitute z=exp(i theta/2)u and mu=kappa exp(i theta): v=exp(-i theta/2)f(z)=u+kappa conjugate(u). Thus g:C->C is the same real-linear map in rotated input/output coordinates, not a claim that f itself is axis aligned.

F3 and proof step 1.2 give g(x+iy)=(1+kappa)x+i(1-kappa)y. A radius-R circle therefore has horizontal semiaxis R(1+kappa), vertical semiaxis R(1-kappa); for R=1 these are exactly Statement (b). The drawing uses kappa=1/3: source R=1.3, target horizontal 1.7333 and vertical 0.8667, rounded geometric coordinates consistent with 4R/3 and 2R/3.

By real-linearity and invertibility (F1, proof 3.1), source inner radius 0.65=R/2 maps to ellipse semiaxes 0.8667 and 0.4333, half the outer semiaxes. Both panels use even-odd fill between nested boundaries; the centre remains unfilled. Dashed boundary curves are excluded, as specified by def-complex-annulus Definition and Remarks. The arrow g sends the left open ring to the right open ring.

Both diagonal factors 1+kappa and 1-kappa are positive; determinant 1-kappa^2>0 (F1), so no reflection or swapped major axis is asserted. The caption explicitly limits the picture to finite positive radii and distinguishes the schematic r/R=1/2 from the statement numerical annulus. Puncture and infinity cases remain exactly those of proof step 3.1 and are not illustrated.
The original proof is preserved byte-for-byte and uses F1-F5 and numbered steps, with no reference to the new figure. The Remarks explicitly state that the proof is independent of the illustration.
